deck: The Florence most visitors never see. It’s at its best once the crowds go home, and that’s when most of these happen.

doors.p: The Accademia to yourself after the doors shut, with a violinist and a soprano. No lines and no crowd around the statue, just you and David.
A private walk along the cathedral’s rooftop. Most people only climb the dome, and timed slots sell out weeks ahead. This is a different way up.
A private sunset cruise under the Ponte Vecchio, as the city turns gold. It’s the best view of Florence, from the one place most visitors never stand.
The Medici stone workshop, opened just for you. The craftsmen still work in hardstone inlay the way they did for the Medici, and you get to watch them do it.
A custom experience that isn’t open to the public, in the city where the house began.
A half-day in a working Florentine bottega, learning the technique behind the walls you’ve been staring at all week. You leave with one of your own.
Heading to Tuscany next? A driver takes you out to the wineries, so you can actually enjoy the tastings, and on to your next hotel.
